posts.name: Humble-Knight
posts.cooked:
Had the most boring and most interesting game against Dawn in order to unlock Bomber Blade. Had Legacy, Tempest, AZ, Wraith, and Haka on my team, and as you can imagine I had no trouble with anything. I had Legacy and Tempest healing for the first half of the game, smoke bomb shenanigans for the second half and overall it was a blow out. What was interesting was how long it took to get to sweat and tears. They came up in the same Infrared Eyepiece so I had to sift through roughly another third of the deck after I put out sweat (a mistake, but not a dibilitating one) to get tears. When she finally did come out, I took the most damage I took all game then got ready to smash them. I had Dawn in the teens all game so I had no problem getting the damage I needed to end it but I did go out of my way to have a little fun.

Tempest and AZ took care of the citizens for the unlock, so I saw how close I could get AZ to dying to thermal shockwave. Got him to 8 HP, more if tempest hadn't finished of 2 citizens, from 28 HP. Used that damage to kill legacy. then I used a inventory barrage on wraith with 1 equipment less than max. Killed wraith immediately. Ended it with a 17 card haka of battle plus a 8 card savage mana. 

Easiest Dawn game I have ever played and also the longest. Who wants to draw out a game against Dawn?

posts.name: Chromium_Man
posts.cooked:
If anyone is having trouble getting Blood, Sweat, and Tears out at the same time, here's a method I used that was pretty effective:

I played Legacy, SSTachyon, Ra, Visionary, and Tempest.

I used SSTachyon to Experiment on Dawn's deck.  Best case scenario, I would pull two Citizens out of turn and if they weren't Blood, Sweat, or Tears, they were dead.  If I pulled one of the three and a non-Citizen card, they would go to the trash where Visionary could use Suggestion to put one back on top or Return with the Dawn would put them back in play.  I could also use Precognition to try to get one of the main targets in play.  Incidentally, I killed off Tears the second she came out so I wouldn't have to discard a thousand cards.  On the turn before the unlock, I used Suggestion to put her on top to minimize the damage she would do.

By the time I got all three out at the same time, Dawn had 5 ongoings in play, so Drawn to the Flame pretty much cleared the board and got me the unlock.  As an aside, Precognition and Experiment are a great combination.  On one turn I used Precognition to put Devastating Aurora and a card with no matching keywords on the bottom of the deck, then discarded them both with Experiment.

posts.name: seesome
posts.cooked:
I just unlocked Cosmic Omnitron! 

Playing SS Tachyon, Fanatic, RC Wraith, & Bunker vs. Voss (normal) in Megalopolis.

The unlock happened when RC Wraith used a Throwing Knife to take out the TCF Conqueror (which had been out for more than one round already and was down to 1HP). In the turn immediately prior to that, Fanatic had used Wrathful Retribution to take out an undamaged TCF Stalwart in a single-shot (the Stalwart had just come out that round).

I had been pretty sure that other folks had already tried taking out both ships in a single round, so I wasn't even focused on that [I was trying to test having Tachyon used two Research Grants in a single turn (via Embolden) as I was figuring that Cosmic Omni was reborn in Meridith's lab].  

So both ships were taken out in the same round, but not on the same turn. One had taken previous damage, one was hit with a single-shot the round it came out.  RC Wraith hadn't even finished using her Knives yet. Other state info, since I'm not sure hat might have been relevant:  RC Wraith had only her Knives and the Belt in play. Voss had nothing besides the Conqueror in play (having lost the Stalwart and a minon the previos turn).

![](upload://kJKxIorshsU7aARKJhHOxKDcVvI.jpeg)

posts.name: seesome
posts.cooked:
Sorry for the late details, I got caught with some RL stuff at home moments asfter posting the tweet about the unlock.

Do we have a third yet for destroying both ships in the same round in Megaopolis to confirm that we're not missing anything?

As for the story connection:

I was specifically experimenting with Voss in Megalopolis and here's why.  Fighting Omni to unlock Cosmi, didn't make story sense.  According to the bio info on the Wiki, Omni had already been defeated and Cosmi was "reborn" while in Tachy's lab when a "cosmic entity" poked at the Omni parts.  So I figured that, just as Bomber Blade was messing around when heroes were fighting Dawn, perhaps the battle with Voss drew an entity's attention to Earth; and the battle was in Megalopolis as that made the most sense for where the lab would be located.

As I said above, I wasn't even trying for both ships as I thought others had done that already.  I was trying to trigger something with the Research Grant card (representing the lab) in Megalopois vs Voss.

posts.name: seesome
posts.cooked:
Also, I'll chime in with a vote in favor of the unlocks. Not because I found two of them first, but because the hunt made for a fun 30 hours.  Now that the info is out there, unlocking the heroes is pretty easy.  The villians are a bit harder, but it mostly just gives you a direction to play rather than just using randomize.

If you had to unlock the expansion packs, that would be annoying.  But as all you really get from the variants is a different power for a hero (rather than a full new deck, character, environment or villain), this was fine with me.
